metadata.name: DISA STIG for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9
metadata.description: Security Technical Implementation Guide for RHEL 9 based on DISA STIG benchmark
metadata.author: DISA

profile.name: STIG
profile.description: DISA Security Technical Implementation Guide - All severity levels

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must be a vendor-supported release
rules.rule_description: An operating system release is considered 'supported' if the vendor continues to provide security patches for the product. With an unsupported release, it will not be possible to resolve security issues discovered in the system software.

assessment.detection_step: Verify that the version of RHEL 9 is vendor supported

remediation.remediation_step: Upgrade to a supported version of RHEL 9.

context.rationale: Running an unsupported OS version leaves the system vulnerable to known security issues without patches.
context.impact: Critical - No security patches available for unsupported versions

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 vendor packaged system security patches and updates must be installed and up to date
rules.rule_description: Installing software updates is a fundamental mitigation against the exploitation of publicly known vulnerabilities. If the most recent security patches and updates are not installed, unauthorized users may take advantage of weaknesses in the unpatched software.

assessment.detection_step: Check for available security updates using dnf or subscription-manager

remediation.remediation_step: Install all available security updates using: sudo dnf update --security

context.rationale: Unpatched systems are vulnerable to known exploits and CVEs.

rules.rule_name: The systemd Ctrl-Alt-Delete burst key sequence in RHEL 9 must be disabled
rules.rule_description: A locally logged-on user who presses Ctrl-Alt-Delete when at the console can reboot the system. If accidentally pressed, as could happen in the case of mixed OS environment, this can create the risk of short-term loss of availability of systems due to unintentional reboot.

assessment.detection_step: Verify the Ctrl-Alt-Delete burst key sequence is disabled in systemd
assessment.expected_value: ctrl-alt-del-burst action should be disabled or set to ignore

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/systemd/system/ctrl-alt-del.target to disable the key sequence: ln -sf /dev/null /etc/systemd/system/ctrl-alt-del.target

context.rationale: Preventing accidental or intentional system reboots via Ctrl-Alt-Delete improves system availability.
context.impact: Medium - Could prevent accidental reboots in multi-OS environments

rules.rule_name: The x86 Ctrl-Alt-Delete key sequence must be disabled on RHEL 9
rules.rule_description: A locally logged-on user who presses Ctrl-Alt-Delete when at the console can reboot the system. If accidentally pressed, this can create the risk of short-term loss of availability of systems due to unintentional reboot.

assessment.detection_step: Verify Ctrl-Alt-Delete is disabled in systemd configuration
assessment.expected_value: Unit ctrl-alt-del.target could not be found or is masked

context.rationale: Disabling Ctrl-Alt-Delete prevents accidental or malicious system reboots.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must disable the ability of systemd to spawn an interactive boot process
rules.rule_description: Using interactive or recovery boot, the console user could disable auditing, firewalls, or other services, weakening system security.

assessment.detection_step: Verify that GRUB 2 is configured to disable interactive boot
assessment.expected_value: No output (systemd.confirm_spawn should not be present)

context.rationale: Interactive boot allows bypassing of security controls at boot time.
context.impact: High - Could allow bypassing of security services

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must require a unique superusers name upon booting into single-user and maintenance modes
rules.rule_description: Having a nondefault grub superuser username makes password-guessing attacks less effective.

assessment.detection_step: Verify that GRUB superuser is configured with a non-default username

remediation.remediation_step: Configure a non-default GRUB superuser in /etc/grub.d/01_users and regenerate grub.cfg

context.rationale: Default usernames make brute-force attacks easier.
context.impact: High - Protects boot loader from unauthorized access

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must require a boot loader superuser password
rules.rule_description: To mitigate the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive information by entities that have been issued certificates by DOD-approved PKIs, all DOD systems must be properly configured to enforce strict authentication requirements.

assessment.detection_step: Verify that GRUB has a superuser password configured

remediation.remediation_step: Set a GRUB superuser password using grub2-setpassword and regenerate grub.cfg

context.rationale: Boot loader password prevents unauthorized modification of boot parameters.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 /boot/grub2/grub.cfg file must be group-owned by root
rules.rule_description: The 'root' group is a highly privileged group. Furthermore, the group-owner of this file should not have any access privileges anyway.

assessment.detection_step: Verify group ownership of grub.cfg

context.rationale: Unauthorized group ownership could allow modification of boot configuration.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 /boot/grub2/grub.cfg file must be owned by root
rules.rule_description: The /boot/grub2/grub.cfg file stores sensitive system configuration. Protection of this file is critical for system security.

assessment.detection_step: Verify ownership of grub.cfg

context.rationale: Unauthorized ownership could allow modification of boot configuration.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must check the GPG signature of software packages originating from external software repositories before installation
rules.rule_description: Changes to any software components can have significant effects on the overall security of the operating system. This requirement ensures the software has not been tampered with and has been signed by a trusted vendor.

assessment.detection_step: Verify GPG signature checking is enabled for all repositories
assessment.expected_value: No output (all repos should have gpgcheck=1)

remediation.remediation_step: Set gpgcheck=1 in all repository files under /etc/yum.repos.d/

context.rationale: GPG signatures ensure package authenticity and integrity.
context.impact: Critical - Prevents installation of tampered packages

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must check the GPG signature of locally installed software packages before installation
rules.rule_description: Changes to any software components can have significant effects on the overall security of the operating system. This requirement ensures the software has not been tampered with.

assessment.detection_step: Verify local package GPG signature checking is enabled

context.rationale: Local package GPG checking prevents installation of unverified packages.
context.impact: High - Prevents installation of tampered local packages

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must have GPG signature verification enabled for all software repositories
rules.rule_description: Changes to any software components can have significant effects on the overall security of the operating system.

assessment.detection_step: Verify all repositories have GPG checking enabled
assessment.expected_value: All repositories should show gpgcheck: yes

remediation.remediation_step: Enable gpgcheck for all repositories in /etc/yum.repos.d/

context.rationale: GPG verification ensures package authenticity across all repositories.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must not have a File Transfer Protocol (FTP) server package installed
rules.rule_description: The FTP service provides an unencrypted remote access that does not provide for the confidentiality and integrity of user passwords or the remote session.

assessment.detection_step: Verify FTP server packages are not installed
assessment.expected_value: Error: No matching Packages to list

remediation.remediation_step: Remove FTP server packages: dnf remove vsftpd proftpd pure-ftpd

context.rationale: FTP transmits credentials in plaintext and should be replaced with SFTP or SCP.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must not have a Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) server package installed
rules.rule_description: Removing the tftp-server package decreases the risk of the accidental or intentional activation of tftp services.

assessment.detection_step: Verify TFTP server package is not installed
assessment.expected_value: Error: No matching Packages to list

remediation.remediation_step: Remove TFTP server: dnf remove tftp-server

context.rationale: TFTP provides no authentication and transmits data unencrypted.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must not have the sendmail package installed
rules.rule_description: The sendmail software was not developed with security in mind, and its design prevents it from being effectively contained by SELinux. Postfix must be used instead.

assessment.detection_step: Verify sendmail package is not installed
assessment.expected_value: Error: No matching Packages to list

remediation.remediation_step: Remove sendmail and install postfix: dnf remove sendmail && dnf install postfix

context.rationale: Sendmail has a history of security vulnerabilities and poor SELinux integration.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must not have the rsh-server package installed
rules.rule_description: The rsh-server service provides unencrypted remote access service, which does not provide for the confidentiality and integrity of user passwords or the remote session and has very weak authentication.

assessment.detection_step: Verify rsh-server package is not installed
assessment.expected_value: Error: No matching Packages to list

remediation.service_impact: RSH services will be unavailable - use SSH instead

context.rationale: RSH protocols transmit credentials in plaintext and have weak authentication.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must not have the telnet-server package installed
rules.rule_description: It is detrimental for operating systems to provide, or install by default, functionality exceeding requirements or mission objectives.

assessment.detection_step: Verify telnet-server package is not installed
assessment.expected_value: Error: No matching Packages to list

remediation.service_impact: Telnet service will be unavailable - use SSH instead

context.rationale: Telnet transmits all data including passwords in plaintext.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must not have the ypserv package installed
rules.rule_description: The NIS service provides an unencrypted authentication service, which does not provide for the confidentiality and integrity of user passwords or the remote session.

assessment.detection_step: Verify ypserv package is not installed
assessment.expected_value: Error: No matching Packages to list

context.rationale: NIS is an insecure legacy authentication service.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must use a separate file system for /tmp
rules.rule_description: The /tmp partition is used as temporary storage by many programs. Placing /tmp in its own partition enables the setting of more restrictive mount options, which can help protect programs that use it.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /tmp is on a separate filesystem
assessment.expected_value: Separate mount point for /tmp should be present

remediation.remediation_step: Create a separate partition for /tmp and configure it in /etc/fstab with nodev,nosuid,noexec options

context.rationale: Separate /tmp partition allows restrictive mount options and prevents resource exhaustion attacks.
context.impact: Medium - Improves filesystem security and stability

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must mount /dev/shm with the nodev option
rules.rule_description: The nodev mount option causes the system to not interpret character or block special devices. Executing character or block special devices from untrusted file systems increases the opportunity for nonprivileged users to attain unauthorized administrative access.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /dev/shm is mounted with nodev option

remediation.remediation_step: Add nodev option to /dev/shm in /etc/fstab: tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec 0 0

context.rationale: Prevents creation of device files in /dev/shm which could be exploited.
context.impact: Medium - Prevents privilege escalation via device files

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must mount /dev/shm with the noexec option
rules.rule_description: The noexec mount option causes the system to not execute binary files. This option must be used for mounting any file system not containing approved binary files.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /dev/shm is mounted with noexec option

context.rationale: Prevents execution of binaries from /dev/shm which is a common attack vector.
context.impact: Medium - Prevents code execution from shared memory

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must mount /dev/shm with the nosuid option
rules.rule_description: The nosuid mount option causes the system to not execute setuid and setgid files with owner privileges.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /dev/shm is mounted with nosuid option

context.rationale: Prevents privilege escalation via SUID binaries in /dev/shm.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 /etc/group- file must have mode 0644 or less permissive
rules.rule_description: The /etc/group- file is a backup file of /etc/group, and as such, contains information regarding groups that are configured on the system.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /etc/group- file permissions

context.rationale: Restricting access to group backup file prevents unauthorized group information disclosure.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 /etc/gshadow file must have mode 0000
rules.rule_description: The /etc/gshadow file contains group password hashes. Protection of this file is critical for system security.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /etc/gshadow file permissions

context.rationale: Group password hashes must be protected from unauthorized access.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 /etc/passwd file must have mode 0644 or less permissive
rules.rule_description: If the /etc/passwd file is writable by a group-owner or the world the risk of its compromise is increased.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /etc/passwd file permissions

context.rationale: Restricting write access to passwd file prevents unauthorized user modifications.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 /etc/passwd- file must have mode 0644 or less permissive
rules.rule_description: The /etc/passwd- file is a backup file of /etc/passwd, and as such, contains information about the users that are configured on the system.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /etc/passwd- file permissions

context.rationale: Protecting passwd backup file prevents user information disclosure.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 /etc/shadow- file must have mode 0000
rules.rule_description: The /etc/shadow- file is a backup file of /etc/shadow, and as such, contains the list of local system accounts and password hashes.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /etc/shadow- file permissions

context.rationale: Password hash backup must be protected from all unauthorized access.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 SSHD must not allow blank passwords
rules.rule_description: If an account has an empty password, anyone could log on and run commands with the privileges of that account. Accounts with empty passwords should never be used in production environments.

assessment.detection_step: Verify SSH does not permit blank passwords

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: PermitEmptyPasswords no

context.rationale: Blank passwords provide no authentication and allow unauthorized access.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must not allow unattended or automatic logon via the graphical user interface
rules.rule_description: Failure to restrict system access to authenticated users negatively impacts operating system security.

assessment.detection_step: Verify automatic login is disabled

context.rationale: Automatic login bypasses authentication requirements.

rules.rule_name: The root account must be the only account having unrestricted access to RHEL 9 system
rules.rule_description: An account has root authority if it has a user identifier (UID) of 0. Multiple accounts with a UID of 0 afford more opportunity for potential intruders to guess a password.

assessment.detection_step: Verify only root has UID 0

remediation.remediation_step: Change the UID of any non-root account with UID 0 or remove the account
remediation.service_impact: Affected users will lose root access

context.rationale: Multiple UID 0 accounts increase attack surface and audit complexity.
context.impact: Critical - Ensures single point of root access control

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must use a Linux Security Module configured to enforce limits on system services
rules.rule_description: Without verification of the security functions, security functions may not operate correctly and the failure may go unnoticed.

assessment.detection_step: Verify SELinux is enabled and enforcing

remediation.remediation_step: Enable SELinux in enforcing mode: Edit /etc/selinux/config and set SELINUX=enforcing
remediation.service_impact: May require policy adjustments for applications

context.rationale: SELinux provides mandatory access control to limit service capabilities.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must not allow blank or null passwords
rules.rule_description: If an account has an empty password, anyone could log in and run commands with the privileges of that account.

assessment.detection_step: Verify system does not allow null passwords
assessment.expected_value: No output (no accounts with empty passwords)

remediation.remediation_step: Set a password for any account with an empty password field: passwd <username>
remediation.service_impact: Users will need to use new passwords

context.rationale: Empty passwords provide no authentication protection.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must enable FIPS mode
rules.rule_description: Use of weak or untested encryption algorithms undermines the purposes of utilizing encryption to protect data.

assessment.detection_step: Verify FIPS mode is enabled

remediation.service_impact: Cryptographic libraries will use FIPS-validated modules

context.rationale: FIPS mode ensures only approved cryptographic algorithms are used.
context.impact: Critical - Required for compliance in many environments

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 groups must have unique Group ID (GID)
rules.rule_description: To ensure accountability and prevent unauthenticated access, groups must be identified uniquely to prevent potential misuse and compromise of the system.

assessment.detection_step: Check for duplicate GIDs

remediation.remediation_step: Edit /etc/group and provide each group with a unique GID
remediation.service_impact: File ownership may need to be updated

context.rationale: Duplicate GIDs can cause confusion and security issues with file access.

rules.rule_name: RHEL 9 must have the sudo package installed
rules.rule_description: sudo is a program designed to allow a system administrator to give limited root privileges to users and log root activity.

assessment.detection_step: Verify sudo package is installed

context.rationale: Sudo provides controlled privilege escalation and audit logging.
